title: Make the tool usable
subtitle: Hand off the report you built with a clear way to check it.
courseLabel: Harness in practice · Tutorial 5 of 6 · Deliver
coursePath: Turn an idea into a useful result
Decide whether to trust the report
Make it work for your needs

sections.title: Hand off the report you built
sections.intro: Start with the HTML report and the evidence you just reviewed.
sections.html:
Open $PRACTICE/activity-report.html. Your handoff will show the result, the input it came from and the check you performed in Decide whether to trust the report.

If you still need a report, return to Build your first report or use the optional checked example in the next section.
presenterNotes: Have learners reuse their report and task evidence when available.

sections.title: Gather the files for your handoff
sections.intro: Use the report and original sample CSV from your practice project.
sections.html:
• HTML report $PRACTICE/activity-report.html
  • Sample CSV $PRACTICE/project/data/activity.csv
  • Your review note or the relevant outcomes from the saved task
Optional fresh start with the checked example

Download the checked example ZIP and extract it into a new folder. Open a terminal in the folder containing report.py and data/activity.csv. The example instructions list the Python requirements and runnable commands.
presenterNotes: Keep the checked example available for people starting from scratch.

sections.title: Show how to open or recreate the report
sections.intro: Give the recipient the report path first.
sections.html:
Ask the recipient to open the supplied HTML file in a browser. If they are running the checked ZIP from a new extraction, use the command below from the folder containing report.py. It writes activity-report.html beside the script.

Optional HTML command for the checked example

Expect Saved report to activity-report.html. If that name is already in use, choose an unused name with --output, then open the new file.
presenterNotes: Opening the existing report is the main path. Use the ZIP command only in the checked example folder.

sections.title: Give the recipient one way to check it
sections.intro: Share an expected result the recipient can find in the HTML.
sections.html:
Ask the recipient to find six entries and 270 minutes, then show how the four Orion rows add up to 180 minutes. Cite the original CSV and the probe outcomes you inspected in lesson 4.

Optional text output for the checked example

From the checked example folder, print a text report with this command. Compare it with the expected text output.
presenterNotes: One concrete comparison makes the handoff usable. Leave extra checks available as references.

sections.title: Try a separate input copy
sections.intro: Optional practice if you want to see how the report responds to a change.
sections.html:
Change one row and compare the result

In the course environment, use the PRACTICE path from lesson 2. Copy $PRACTICE/project/data/activity.csv to a new $PRACTICE/activity-practice.csv. In the copy, change Lumen’s Documentation entry from 30 to 45 minutes.

Predict the result before running the command: six entries, 285 minutes overall and 105 minutes for Lumen. Choose unused input-copy and output filenames, and update the command if you chose different names.

Open the new HTML file. Compare its actual numbers with your prediction.
presenterNotes: Place the optional input copy and output beside the project so the protected inputs stay intact.

sections.title: Write a short handoff
sections.intro: Give the recipient a file to open, a result to look for and the evidence you used.
sections.html:
Example handoff

Open activity-report.html in your browser. Look for six entries and 270 minutes. Compare Orion’s 180 minutes with its four rows in the attached CSV. I checked that subtotal and inspected both saved reporting probes.

Use your own result and observed checks in the handoff. Include the checked example ZIP only if the recipient needs to recreate the report independently.

This optional note stays in your browser profile and site.
presenterNotes: Check that the handoff uses the learner’s actual report and results.

sections.title: Check that someone can use the handoff
sections.intro: Read your note as a recipient who has never seen the practice folder.
sections.html:
Check that you can find the report, locate one number and see what the original check covered. If a recipient needs to recreate the file, include the checked example instructions and explain how to choose a fresh output filename.

Next: Open Make it work for your needs to identify one improvement.
presenterNotes: Use the check to confirm that the recipient can preserve an existing report.

check.question: A previous activity-report.html already exists. What is the supported next action?

options.text: Keep it and use an unused --output filename, then open that same new file.
options.feedback: Correct. The reporting tool creates a new file and refuses to overwrite an existing destination.

options.text: Run the same command again and expect it to replace the old report.
options.feedback: The existing-file refusal is intentional. Select a new output path and preserve the previous result.
